description: Assignment to .innerHTML — DOM XSS sink
Assignment to .outerHTML — DOM XSS sink
Element.insertAdjacentHTML(...) — DOM XSS sink
document.write(...) — DOM XSS sink
document.writeln(...) — DOM XSS sink
eval() — direct code execution
new Function(...) — code execution from string
setTimeout('code', ...) — code execution from string
setInterval('code', ...) — code execution from string
Assignment to location.href — navigation sink
location.assign(...) — navigation sink
location.replace(...) — navigation sink
window.open(...) — opens URL, can be javascript:
postMessage(...) — cross-origin send
iframe srcdoc=... — embedded HTML sink
React dangerouslySetInnerHTML prop — bypasses JSX escaping
$.html(...) — jQuery DOM injection (also matches some non-jQuery .html() — false positives possible)
$.append(...) — jQuery DOM injection (also matches DOM Element.append() which auto-escapes strings — false positives possible)
$.before(...) — jQuery DOM injection (also matches DOM Element.before() — false positives possible)
$.after(...) — jQuery DOM injection (also matches DOM Element.after() — false positives possible)
fetch(...) — outbound network; SSRF / open-redirect when URL is attacker-controlled
fetch(`...`) / fetch("...") / fetch('...') — fetch with template literal or string-looking first arg; SSRF or open-redirect when interpolated values are attacker-controlled
XMLHttpRequest.open(method, url, ...) — second arg is the URL; SSRF when attacker-controlled
axios(...) / axios.{get,post,put,delete,patch,request,head,options}(...) — HTTP call; SSRF when URL is attacker-controlled
Property read assigned to .innerHTML — gadget for prototype-pollution → XSS (rhs is identifier/member, not string literal)
Property read passed to eval() — gadget for prototype-pollution → code execution
Property read passed to setTimeout/setInterval — gadget for prototype-pollution → code execution when value resolves to a string
Dynamic require() with property read — gadget for prototype-pollution → RCE in Node.js
child_process.exec / execSync / execFileSync — OS command injection (RCE)
child_process.spawn / spawnSync / execFile — lower than exec (no shell) but still dangerous with user-controlled args
fs operations / require() with user-controlled path — path traversal / LFI
MongoDB/Mongoose query with user-controlled object — NoSQL injection
raw SQL via .query/.raw/.run with template literal — SQL injection (string concatenation / interpolation)
Node http/https/got/node-fetch/superagent request — SSRF when URL is user-controlled
Express res.render() with user-controlled template name or data — SSTI / XSS
Express res.send / res.end / res.write — reflected XSS in SSR HTML responses
Express res.redirect() with user-controlled URL — open redirect
Express res.cookie() with user-controlled name or value
Angular DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrust* — explicitly bypasses XSS protection
Angular [innerHTML] / [outerHTML] template binding with user-controlled value
Angular document.execCommand or Renderer2.setProperty with user-controlled markup
Vue v-html directive with user-controlled value — bypasses Vue XSS protection
Vue render function h() / createVNode / resolveComponent with user-controlled innerHTML prop
Electron shell.openExternal() with user-controlled URL — can launch arbitrary apps
Electron webContents.executeJavaScript() with user-controlled code string — RCE in main process
